variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Model serving patterns are reusable ways to turn trained model artifacts into dependable prediction services. They define how a request is admitted, queued, batched, routed to a compatible model replica, executed, observed, and either completed or rejected.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Start by choosing the request contract”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Synchronous online
pairs.detail: A gateway holds the connection until one prediction finishes.
pairs.explanation: A gateway holds the connection until one prediction finishes. Tight tail latency, cancellation, bounded retries, and load shedding matter more than maximum batch size.

pairs.label: Asynchronous job
pairs.detail: Durable work can wait longer and form large batches.
pairs.explanation: Durable work can wait longer and form large batches. The contract needs job identity, deduplication, progress, result retention, and explicit expiry.

pairs.label: Streaming response
pairs.explanation: The service emits incremental results. Time to first result, inter-result cadence, backpressure, disconnect propagation, and partial-failure semantics become first-class.

pairs.label: Composed inference
pairs.detail: Preprocessing, retrieval, models, and policy checks form a graph.
pairs.explanation: Preprocessing, retrieval, models, and policy checks form a graph. Each stage needs its own deadline, ownership, observability, and fallback behavior.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is admit only work the fleet can finish inside an explicit contract.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Synchronous online: A gateway holds the connection until one prediction finishes. Asynchronous job: Durable work can wait longer and form large batches. Streaming response: The service emits incremental results. Composed inference: Preprocessing, retrieval, models, and policy checks form a graph.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Choose a pattern from workload shape”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Dedicated replica pool
pairs.detail: Each pool owns one version and a narrow workload.
pairs.explanation: Each pool owns one version and a narrow workload. Isolation and debugging are simple, but low-volume models can strand expensive memory.

pairs.label: Multi-model worker
pairs.detail: Workers load several artifacts or swap them from a model cache.
pairs.explanation: Workers load several artifacts or swap them from a model cache. Utilization improves when routing preserves locality, but cold loads and eviction become tail-latency risks.

pairs.label: Model ensemble
pairs.detail: Several models or transforms execute as one declared graph.
pairs.explanation: Several models or transforms execute as one declared graph. It simplifies the client contract while coupling stage deadlines, version compatibility, and failure behavior.

pairs.label: Specialized serving pools
pairs.detail: Route preprocessing, embedding, prefill, decode, or policy work to different pools when their hardware and scheduling needs differ.
pairs.explanation: Route preprocessing, embedding, prefill, decode, or policy work to different pools when their hardware and scheduling needs differ. Network transfer and cross-pool failure are the cost.

variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Dedicated replica pool: Each pool owns one version and a narrow workload. Multi-model worker: Workers load several artifacts or swap them from a model cache. Model ensemble: Several models or transforms execute as one declared graph. Specialized serving pools: Route preprocessing, embedding, prefill, decode, or policy work to different pools when their hardware and scheduling needs differ.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Model serving patterns are reusable ways to turn trained model artifacts into dependable prediction services. They define how a request is admitted, queued, batched, routed to a compatible model replica, executed, observed, and either completed or rejected.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Treat caches as correctness boundaries”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Artifact cache
pairs.detail: Stores immutable model files by digest.
pairs.explanation: Stores immutable model files by digest. Verify integrity before activation and keep the version manifest separate from a mutable path or tag.

pairs.label: Resident model cache
pairs.explanation: Avoids model-load latency. Routing, eviction, pinning, and memory fragmentation determine whether a request reaches a warm worker.

pairs.label: Feature or embedding cache
pairs.detail: Keys need source version, transformation version, authorization scope, and expiry.
pairs.explanation: Keys need source version, transformation version, authorization scope, and expiry. Stale features can produce valid-looking but wrong predictions.

pairs.label: Prediction cache
pairs.detail: Safe only for deterministic or explicitly reusable results.
pairs.explanation: Safe only for deterministic or explicitly reusable results. Include model, adapter, decoding parameters, policy version, tenant boundary, and normalized input in the key.

pairs.label: Observe pressure
pairs.detail: Measure queue age, queued work units, active concurrency, deadline risk, cache misses, and accelerator memory by model and priority.

pairs.label: Compute desired capacity
pairs.detail: Convert forecast demand into warm replicas or accelerator slots at a measured utilization target with failure headroom.
pairs.explanation: Convert forecast demand into warm replicas or accelerator slots at a measured utilization target with failure headroom.

pairs.label: Provision and warm
pairs.detail: Schedule hardware, fetch an immutable artifact, allocate runtime memory, run warm-up inputs, and pass readiness before routing traffic.
pairs.explanation: Schedule hardware, fetch an immutable artifact, allocate runtime memory, run warm-up inputs, and pass readiness before routing traffic.

pairs.label: Drain deliberately
pairs.detail: Stop new admission, finish or cancel bounded work, release model state, and preserve enough warm floor for the next burst.
